newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 23.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Football League is likely to make a long term commitment to State of Origin matches following successful weekend games in Perth and Adelaide. The AFL's major sponsor Coca Cola is keen for Origin to continue given the enthusiasm of the players and the size of the audience it draws. Page 19.

Australian Football League team Collingwood are resigned to eventually not playing any games at their traditional ground at Victoria Park due to poor facilities. AFL chief executive officer Wayne Jackson said the AFL might not schedule any games at the ground next year. Page 21.

Racing driver Geoff Brabham finished Round Three the new leader of the Australian Super Touring Championship, after starting the day's first race at the back of the grid on the Calder Park circuit yesterday. Brabham leads the championship on 74 points, two clear of team-mate Paul Morris. Page 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker refused to speculate yesterday as to how the pay-TV deal between Rupert Murdoch and Kerry Packer would affect major sponsors Optus, but did concede that Optus had not signed up for 1998. Page 26.

The Australian rugby team management decided last night not to cite French captain Abdel Benazzi for kneeing Wallaby five-eighth Tim Horan in the back during Saturday's 29-15 Australian victory. Horan is in serious doubt for the second Test at the weekend Page 31.

Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker will view video today of an incident where Gold Coast Chargers second-rower Chris Nahi allegedly bit Balmain hooker Darren Senter on the arm during the Chargers 22-20 victory on Saturday. However, Sener has declined to make a formal complaint. Page 26.
THE AGE

Brisbane Broncos rugby league coach Wayne Bennett has expressed concern for the welfare of rugby league in the Northern Hemisphere following his team's 76-0 defeat of Halifax in a World Club Challenge game yesterday. Page 16.

The Melbourne Phoenix remain undefeated in the national netball league after beating the Adelaide Ravens 62-51 at the weekend. The Phoenix have now won seven games and drawn one, putting them three points clear of nearest rivals - the Adelaide T'birds. Page 20.

St Kilda AFL player Nicky Winmar believes he has overcome the personal difficulties that saw him dropped from the senior team for missing training. Winmar put in strong performances in his last two club games and the State of Origin last weekend for Westen Australia. Page 6.
THE HERALD SUN

Harness Racing Victoria chairman Ian McEwen and board members will meet Sky Channel chief Warren Wilson on Friday to negotiate a deal to have Victorian harness racing broadcast on Foxtel and Optus Vision as early as October, though McEwen yesterday pledged to have free-to-air racing telecast until June next year. Page 79.

The Young Socceroos will go into the final Group E match of the World Youth Cup in Malaysia tonight needing at least a draw against former world champions Argentina to stay in the competition, and progress to the knockout phase. Page 81.

Australian Olympian swimmer Scott Miller has vowed not to change his behaviour despite being expelled from the Australian Institute of Sport two weeks ago after being involved in an altercation at a Canberra night-club during a team training camp. Page 79
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Melbourne Cup is likely to be devoid of quality competition from the northern hemisphere for the first time in five years, due to the relatively poor results of horses that have been taken to Australia to contest the race. Page 47.

Twenty-four-year-old Lee Troop qualified for the world half-marathon championship in Slovakia in October with a winning time only four seconds outside the race record in the Australian title held at Lake Macquarie yesterday. Troop ran the course in 63 mintes and 17 seconds. Page 45.

St George fullback Dean Raper will face the Australian Rugby League judiciary today to answer an abuse charge by referee Paul Simpkins, who officiated in the Dragons' loss to Illawarra 10-12, yesterday. Simpkins alleges Raper abused him after the game. Page 33.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
